observations: Photo 0 and Photo 1 show the same solar panel from slightly different angles.
The panel has a grid of dark, rectangular solar cells arranged in a hexagonal pattern.
The frame is black and appears to be made of metal or plastic.
The surface of the cells is reflective, with some light glare and reflections visible.
There is a watermark 'DON KACHI SOLAR ENERGY' overlaid on both photos.
The panel is standing upright, leaning against another similar panel.
No brand name, model number, or specifications are visible on the panel itself.
The background shows a concrete floor and part of another panel to the left.

claims.evidence: Price is not shown in photos; seller's statement only.

risks.risk: The panel may be damaged or defective, such as microcracks in cells, delamination, or poor junction box connections.
risks.proof: A close-up photo of the junction box, wiring, and edges of the cells, showing no cracks, corrosion, or loose connections.
risks.if_unproven: priced as potentially non-functional or low-efficiency

risks.risk: The panel may be counterfeit or of low quality, lacking proper certification (e.g., IEC, CE) or rated for the intended use.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the label or nameplate on the back of the panel showing model, wattage, voltage, and certifications.
risks.if_unproven: priced as unverified quality, possibly lower than standard

risks.risk: The panel may be used or refurbished without disclosure, affecting its lifespan and performance.
risks.proof: A photo showing the back of the panel with the nameplate and any signs of wear, scratches, or previous installations.
risks.if_unproven: priced as used, with potential for reduced efficiency

proof_requests: Close-up of the label on the back of the panel showing the model, wattage, and certifications.
Close-up photo of the junction box and wiring to check for damage or corrosion.
Photo of the back of the panel showing the nameplate and any signs of wear or previous use.
response.reason: The item is known from the photos. What they cannot prove is priced at its worst case until the proof asked for below arrives.
